svg.text: THE UNBOUND PAWN - DETAILED ROOM MAP
Every box is a future editable Godot room scene: TileMap, exits, enemies, objects, reward, and lesson.

g.text: Story: white army collapses, pawn wakes.
Reward: sword. Lesson: face then strike.
First combat: enemies obey pawn rules.
Hub: all districts branch from here.
Teaches: knight windup and L pressure.
Fast room: react to marked landing tiles.
Player learns to cross diagonals safely.
Boss: diagonal waves plus safe gaps.
Teaches: hide from rook line attacks.
Child moves a toy wall out of the way.
Final: pawn and player break checkmate.
1. Each card becomes one room scene under scenes/rooms/. Keep the TileMap, exits, props, enemies, and pickups visible in the editor.
2. Start with T1, T2, T3, and H1. That gives the game a playable opening before we build the boss districts.
3. Do not build all bosses first. Build one full district loop: hub -> normal room -> pressure room -> boss -> reward -> hub shortcut.
4. Use the same 8x5 planning board in this image as a rough gameplay shape, then scale it up in Godot to the real TileMap size.
5. The detailed tile art can change later. The important thing now is room purpose, exits, cover, enemy placement, and player learning.
